clues: This city lies in the west of its district in Uttarakhand, in the north of India. It is a busy town in the old Kumaun lands.
The rain here swings wildly with the seasons of the year. July soaks this town with about 374 mm of rain, while November gets just 5 mm.
In 1815, this town played a major role in the Anglo-Gorkha war. That war won the whole Kumaun region for the British.
This town took its name from the man who founded it long ago. He was a governor who served the kings of Kumaun.
This city is home to one of just thirteen IIM schools in India. These top schools were set up by the state.
